# Module `https`

https - TLS-secured HTTP/1.1 client that layers the `tls` module over the
pure-`http` client.

Imports `network` for the raw TCP connect, `tls` for the encrypted channel, and
`http` for its pure request/parse helpers (the status/header/int parsers and
the shared `HttpResponse` type). Because TLS runs on top of a socket, this
module does its own TLS-aware I/O (reading the same byte shapes the http
client does, but from the SSL stream), then reuses http's parsers to build an
HttpResponse identically to http_get_full. The shared response type is
re-exported so consumers can name it, and `https_selfhost` gives a no-external-
server diagnostic of the whole tls+http wiring.

  https_get(host, port, path) -> String        full GET round-trip -> body
  https_get_full(host, port, path) -> HttpResponse   parsed status/headers/body

<a id="sym-vec-string-"></a>
### `Vec<String>` · fn

```
headers = Vec<String>(), body = "" }
```

Full HTTPS/1.1 GET round-trip. Returns an HttpResponse with the parsed status,
reason, headers, and body; status is -1 if the round-trip could not be
completed (e.g. connection/handshake failure).
Shared round-trip: connect to `connect_ip` on `port`, bring up a TLS session
over it that verifies the peer against the `verify_host` (SNI + hostname check
on verifying contexts), send a GET for `path`, and parse the response. Owns
and frees `ctx`.
socket_open(AF_INET=2, SOCK_STREAM=1, IPPROTO_TCP=6).

### `https_get_full_verified` · fn

```
https_get_full_verified(host<String>, port<Int>, path<String>, ca_pem<String>)<HttpResponse> ->
```

Full HTTPS/1.1 GET round-trip with peer verification. `host` is a hostname:
it is resolved to an IP for the connection while being verified against the
certificate (SNI + hostname check). `ca_pem` pins a CA cert or is "" to use
the system default CA paths.

<a id="sym-https_selfhost"></a>
### `https_selfhost` · fn

```
https_selfhost(cert_pem<String>, key_pem<String>)<Int> ->
```

Diagnostics: stand up a throwaway TLS server that answers one request with a
well-formed response, fetch it over TLS, and report whether the round-trip
parsed as expected. Returns 0 on success, -1 on any failure. Useful as a
self-test of the tls+http wiring without standing up an external server.
